issues.legal_issue: A delay in appealing the dismissal of execution-sale objections should be condoned when the delay is not substantial, the party acted after learning of the dismissal, and the circumstances do not show callous or mala fide conduct.
material_facts: The appellant’s objections to the execution sale were dismissed after it failed to appear to lead evidence, and the sale was confirmed.
The appellant’s first appeal was delayed by about two months and a few days; it sought condonation under Section 5 of the Limitation Act.
The appellant relied on its former advocate’s failure to inform it of the dismissal and said it acted to file an appeal after learning of it.
The Court found that the appellant had taken steps to prosecute the matter, had not been absolutely callous or negligent, and would not have gained from delaying the appeal.
The Court considered that the delay was not so substantial as to warrant dismissal on a technical ground and that the respondent’s inconvenience could be addressed by costs.
The Executing Court had closed the appellant’s evidence, leaving the objections without a determination on their merits.
issues.conclusion: The Court set aside the orders rejecting the appeal as time-barred, condoned the delay, and remitted the objections to the Executing Court for decision on the merits. The appellant was required to pay costs to the respondent as a condition of prosecuting its objections.
issues.legal_principle: Section 5 of the Limitation Act does not prescribe a straight-jacket formula for deciding whether sufficient cause exists; each case must be assessed in light of its facts and the party’s conduct. As a general rule, delay should be condoned unless mala fides are writ large, and courts should endeavour to have matters contested on their merits rather than dismiss them on technicalities. The Court stated that it was unnecessary to address the cited decisions on Section 5. The objections were remitted for consideration under Order 21 Rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure, without any opinion on their merits.

rule.if: appeal_seeks_review_of_rejection_as_time_barred and delay_not_substantial and party_acted_after_learning_of_dismissal and party_took_steps_to_prosecute and not callous_or_mala_fide_conduct

predicates.appeal_seeks_review_of_rejection_as_time: A party brings an appeal challenging the rejection of its appeal as filed out of time.
predicates.delay_not_substantial: The delay in filing the appeal is not so substantial that it warrants dismissal on that ground alone.
predicates.party_acted_after_learning_of_dismissal: The party took steps to appeal after it learned that its objections had been dismissed.
predicates.party_took_steps_to_prosecute: The party had taken steps to pursue the matter before the appeal was filed.
predicates.callous_or_mala_fide_conduct: The party’s conduct in pursuing the matter was callous or showed mala fides.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a time-barred rejection, the delay is not substantial, the party acted after learning of the dismissal and had taken steps to pursue the matter, and its conduct was not callous or mala fide, the delay is condoned and the objections are restored for decision on their merits.
